$comment: Golden set for retrieval evaluation (rag.md).
A FILE, not rows in eval_golden_set, for two reasons. Document UUIDs are
generated per ingest and differ between environments, so a set keyed on them
cannot move between a laptop, CI and production. And a file is reviewable in
a diff by whoever changes retrieval, which is the point of a gate.
The table remains for online/production scoring, which does have stable ids.
Cases are keyed on document TITLE because that is what the ingest pipeline
preserves and what citations render.
For a CRAWLED document the title comes from the registry in
apps/api/src/lib/crawl-registry.ts rather than from the page, and it is identity
rather than description: a document is (source_id, title), so renaming one there
does not rename it here, it starts a second lineage beside the first and
silently breaks whichever case pointed at the old name.
Externally sourced documents are ingested from checked-in snapshots in
eval/external/ rather than from a live fetch. That is deliberate: scoring
retrieval against whatever a publisher happened to have live that morning would
make a regression and an editorial change the same event.
Queries are deliberately phrased the way a founder would ask, not in the
wording of the documents. A golden set that echoes the corpus measures string
matching and flatters every retriever that has ever existed.
NEGATIVE cases (expect_docs: []) are the load-bearing half. They assert the
system RETURNS NOTHING, which is what forces the agent to refuse instead of
grounding an answer in whatever was nearest. A retriever that scores well on
positives and leaks on negatives is worse than useless here: it produces
confident, cited, wrong plans.
The negatives above are BUSINESS-FORMATION topics, far from the corpus in
vocabulary as well as in subject. That is why they pass, and it is also why
they hid a real defect for so long: they only ever tested the easy direction.
`scope_negatives` below is the hard direction, and it is scored separately.
Measured: 'conversion tracking in GA4' scores 0.0211 against a 0.0013
threshold, while the legitimate broad goal 'launch my app and get me to my
first 100 customers' tops out at 0.0018. The bands overlap by 12x.
So these cases do NOT belong in `cases`: putting them there would fail the
retrieval gate permanently for something retrieval cannot be asked to do.
They are the groundedness gate's set, scored by `--gate`, which is a
credentialed, LLM-dependent pass and deliberately NOT the deterministic CI
gate. Add one whenever you find a marketing question the corpus does not
cover; that is now a security task, not a coverage one.
VOCABULARY CASES (`vocab-*`) exist because the corpus decides which words
work. Measured before they were added: 'marketing plan to get registrations'
returned refusing-v0 with nothing above threshold, while the same request
phrased with 'signups' returned a full six-stage plan. At a 1.76x threshold
margin a synonym the corpus lacks is the whole distance between a plan and a
refusal. Two fixes landed together and each of these cases pins both: the
corpus now uses the words people actually use, and `vocabulary.py` rewrites
the remaining variants into corpus terms before retrieval. They are ordinary
positives, because that is what they are: requests the corpus can answer.
MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED HERE. Four negatives were drafted to
guard the vocabulary rules, and three of them are absent on purpose, which is
worth recording rather than quietly dropping. Measured against the live corpus
with decomposition on, threshold 0.0013:
'how do I register my company in the UK'        ICO guide     0.0032
'where do I register a trademark for my brand'  Google Ads    0.0017
'what should I pay my first team members'       influencer    0.0017
They are not filed as cases for the reason `scope_negatives` exists at all:
putting them here would fail the retrieval gate permanently for something
retrieval cannot be asked to do. Each leaks on genuinely related-ish material
(a UK regulator document for a UK question, Google's own trademark policy for
a trademark question, a document about what to pay a collaborator for a
question about what to pay a person). That is the 'right field-ish, wrong
question' shape, which is the groundedness gate's job and not the threshold's.
They also do NOT test what they were drafted to test. `vocabulary.py` runs
before retrieval, and a dry run over every query in this file confirms all
eight negatives and all six scope negatives pass through it UNCHANGED. So the
guards are pinned in tests/test_vocabulary.py, per rule, which is the level a
code rule belongs at. `neg-vat-registration` is kept because it passes and
because it exercises the tax exclusion.
The underlying cause is the one ADR-0009 already names: the local threshold's
1.76x margin 'is not headroom to spend, and the corpus can consume it without
the threshold being able to buy it back'. This change grew the corpus by three
documents and removed seven chunks of navigation chrome from the crawled ones,
and hard adjacent negatives are what got squeezed. Do not answer that by
raising RERANK_LOCAL_MIN_SCORE; rag-knowledge.md measures that as trading a
leak for refusals of legitimate goals at random.
PROMOTED, and worth recording rather than quietly editing: scope-influencer-
rates and scope-affiliate-program were scope negatives until the corpus grew
documents that answer them, and they are now the positives infl-pricing and
aff-structure. A scope negative that has become covered does not merely stop
testing anything, it fails `--gate` on block rate for being answered
correctly. Their replacements (scope-influencer-platforms, scope-affiliate-
networks) keep the same near-miss shape: the corpus covers choosing partners
and structuring commission, and says nothing about which vendor to use.

scope_negatives.query: how do I build a webinar funnel that converts
scope_negatives.notes: Measured leak: 0.0067 local, 0.318 Cohere, both well clear of threshold. Retrieves landing-conversion and content-strategy, neither of which discusses webinars at all. The archetypal case: right field, right vocabulary, wrong question.

scope_negatives.query: how do I set up conversion tracking in GA4
scope_negatives.notes: Measured leak: 0.0211 local, 0.281 Cohere. The strongest leak in the set, outscoring the legitimate broad goal by 12x. What it guards has CHANGED and the case is deliberately kept rather than retired. It used to mean 'measurement is the one stage with no document'; measurement-attribution.md now closes that stage, and that document names no analytics platform anywhere, on purpose. So this now guards the sharper thing: we cover measurement principles, and stretching them into a platform setup question is the failure. Same role scope-ad-specs plays for Google specs against a Meta question.

scope_negatives.query: how do I rank higher in the app store
scope_negatives.notes: Measured leak: 0.0053 local, 0.082 Cohere. ASO shares almost every word with the SEO document and shares none of its mechanics.

scope_negatives.query: what are the character limits for facebook ad headlines
scope_negatives.notes: Still uncovered, but no longer uncovered on purpose, and the distinction matters. The crawl registry now carries Google's responsive search ad format spec, so SOME platform specifics are in the corpus with a real source and a read date. Facebook's are not: the Meta ads guide builds its spec tables in the browser, so a fetch returns navigation, and one attempt stored a menu localised to the crawler's own IP. A confident answer here is therefore still a fabrication, and this case is the thing that would catch the Google document being stretched to cover a question about Meta.

scope_negatives.query: which influencer marketing platform should I use to find creators
scope_negatives.notes: Replaces scope-influencer-rates, which became covered and was promoted to the positive infl-pricing. Same near-miss shape, moved one step along: the corpus now covers how to choose a partner and what to pay them, and says nothing about which vendor or marketplace to use. A gate that waves this through is matching on topic rather than on question.

scope_negatives.query: which affiliate network should I join and how do I get accepted
scope_negatives.notes: Replaces scope-affiliate-program, promoted to aff-structure. The corpus covers structuring a program of your own, including commission and fraud, and says nothing about joining somebody else's network or being approved by one.
